context.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a 30-year-old regional insurer's claims platform via a hybrid architecture. It gradually migrates claim types from the legacy mainframe to Azure while maintaining uninterrupted core operations.]

## Key Elements
- Customers & Brokers: External users submitting claims via web browser.
- Claims Adjusters: Internal staff handling claims via web application.
- New Claims Platform: Azure-hosted containerized application (.NET Core on AKS/App Service).
- Legacy Mainframe: On-premises IBM z/OS COBOL/DB2 system of record.
- Active Directory: On-premises identity provider.
- Notification Service: External SaaS (Twilio SendGrid/Azure Communication Services).
- Telemetry & Monitoring: Azure Application Insights/Azure Monitor.

## Relationships
- Customers/Brokers -> New Claims Platform: HTTPS (Online claim submission, R-01).
- Claims Adjusters -> New Claims Platform: HTTPS (Claim management, R-02, <2s load time).
- New Claims Platform <-> Legacy Mainframe: TLS via VPN/ExpressRoute with mTLS (Claim data proxying).
- New Claims Platform -> Active Directory: OIDC/OAuth 2.0 via Azure AD Connect (Single sign-on, R-07).
- New Claims Platform -> Notification Service: HTTPS REST API (SMS/Email dispatch).
- New Claims Platform -> Telemetry & Monitoring: HTTPS/Native Diagnostics (Metrics and logs).

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service & AKS: Container hosting for the new platform, chosen for rapid feature delivery despite limited cloud experience.
- .NET Core: Backend application framework for high performance and strong enterprise support.
- IBM z/OS & DB2: Legacy system of record retained per 3-year migration constraint.
- Azure Key Vault: Secret management for third-party API keys.
- Azure Application Insights: Managed observability to compensate for team's low cloud experience.

## Rationale
[The hybrid Azure-on-premises architecture decouples the modern web front-end from the rigid legacy mainframe, satisfying performance and security constraints. Incremental claim-type migration minimizes expensive mainframe changes while guaranteeing system consistency and zero data loss.]

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a hybrid cloud platform on Azure West Europe. It ensures seamless claim processing, zero data loss, and rapid rollback capabilities while the legacy system remains the system of record.

## Key Elements
- Customers & Brokers, Claims Adjusters, Customer Support Agents
- Azure API Management (Strangler Fig Router)
- Customer Portal (React SPA in Azure Static Web Apps)
- Adjuster Web Application (React SPA + ASP.NET Core BFF)
- Claims Processing Engine (ASP.NET Core Microservices on Azure Kubernetes Service)
- Anti-Corruption Layer (Azure Functions & Azure Service Bus)
- Azure Cache for Redis
- Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2, On-Premises)
- Azure Active Directory & Key Vault

## Relationships
- Users access portals via HTTPS/REST through Azure API Management.
- Azure API Management routes traffic to the React SPAs, BFF, and Legacy Mainframe via site-to-site VPN/ExpressRoute using mTLS and TLS 1.3.
- Adjuster BFF queries Azure Cache for Redis to serve claims within the <2s SLA.
- Claims Processing Engine and Anti-Corruption Layer use Azure Service Bus topics for event-driven messaging.
- Anti-Corruption Layer synchronizes data with the Legacy Mainframe via restricted batch/interface protocols.

## Technology Stack
- Azure API Management: Manages routing and Strangler Fig pattern for incremental claim migration.
- Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS): Hosts scalable Claims Processing Engine microservices.
- Azure Functions & Azure Service Bus: Powers the Anti-Corruption Layer to insulate against legacy schema changes.
- Azure Cache for Redis: Buffers slow mainframe responses to meet performance SLAs.
- Azure Active Directory & OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect: Centralizes single sign-on and RBAC.

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture uses an Anti-Corruption Layer and Strangler Fig router to isolate the new cloud platform from expensive mainframe dependencies. This design guarantees zero lost claims, supports one-day rollbacks, and fits the team's cloud skill set.

Azure API Management.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old mainframe with a modern Azure cloud platform while maintaining continuous claims processing. It utilizes a hybrid architecture to ensure seamless incremental migration, secure authentication, and rapid rollback capabilities.

## Key Elements
- Customers & Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- Third-Party Partners & InsurTechs
- Azure API Management (Strangler Fig Router)
- Customer Portal (React SPA in Azure Static Web Apps)
- Adjuster Web Application (React SPA + ASP.NET Core BFF)
- Claims Processing Engine (ASP.NET Core Microservices on AKS)
- Anti-Corruption Layer (Azure Functions & Azure Service Bus)
- Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2 on-premise)
- Azure App Configuration & Azure Cache for Redis
- Azure Active Directory & Key Vault

## Relationships
- Customers, Brokers, Adjusters, Partners -> Azure API Management: Accesses services and APIs [HTTPS/REST with TLS 1.3, OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect]
- Azure API Management -> Customer Portal & Adjuster Web Application: Routes traffic [HTTPS]
- Strangler Fig Router Policy -> Routing Configuration Store: Queries live routing rules [HTTPS/REST]
- Strangler Fig Router Policy -> Claims Processing Engine: Routes migrated claims [gRPC / HTTPS]
- Strangler Fig Router Policy -> Legacy Mainframe: Proxies unmigrated claims [site-to-site VPN/ExpressRoute with mTLS]
- Claims Processing Engine -> Anti-Corruption Layer: Translates domain events [Azure Service Bus]

## Technology Stack
- Azure API Management: Acts as Strangler Fig router and gateway, chosen for policy enforcement and routing capabilities.
- ASP.NET Core & Azure Kubernetes Service: Powers microservices for high scalability and modern developer velocity.
- React SPA & Azure Static Web Apps: Delivers performant, responsive UIs for customers and adjusters.
- Azure App Configuration: Enables zero-downtime, dynamic feature-flag routing for instant claim-type rollbacks.
- Azure Active Directory & Key Vault: Handles SSO integration, OAuth 2.0 validation, and secure mTLS certificate management.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates the expensive-to-change mainframe behind an anti-corruption layer while decoupling migration via API management. It guarantees business continuity, sub-second modern UI performance, strict security compliance, and one-day rollbacks.

Customer Portal.analysis:
## Overview
The Customer Portal is a React single-page application hosted on Azure Static Web Apps that provides policyholders and brokers with an intuitive, secure interface for online claim submission and tracking. It acts as the primary user-facing entry point within the hybrid Insurance Claims Modernization platform.

## Key Elements
* Customer Portal (React SPA in Azure Static Web Apps)
* Claim Submission Wizard component
* Claim Tracking Dashboard component
* Broker Portfolio Manager component
* Auth & Session Manager component
* Azure Static Web Apps Built-in Auth
* Azure API Management

## Relationships
* Customer Portal -> Azure Static Web Apps Auth: Manages secure session cookies [HTTPS]
* Claim Submission Wizard -> Azure API Management: Submits claim payloads [HTTPS / REST]
* Broker Portfolio Manager -> Azure API Management: Fetches authorized client claims [HTTPS / REST with JWT]
* Auth & Session Manager -> Azure Active Directory: Acquires tokens [OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect]

## Technology Stack
* React & TypeScript: Core UI framework for maintainable frontend development
* Azure Static Web Apps: Hosting and built-in authentication routing to minimize operational overhead for a cloud-inexperienced team
* Zod & React Hook Form: Client-side validation ensuring robust draft data integrity
* TanStack Query: Lightweight server-state management avoiding complex store libraries
* IndexedDB: Local browser storage for offline-resilient claim draft persistence

## Rationale
This architecture balances stringent security and consistency requirements (R-04, R-07) with the team's low cloud experience by leveraging managed Azure platform features. A lean SPA design avoids unnecessary infrastructure complexity while delivering sub-two-second performance and robust multi-client support for brokers.

Adjuster Web Application.analysis:
## Overview
The Adjuster Web Application modernizes the regional insurer's claims handling workflow while operating within a hybrid cloud architecture. It provides adjusters with a secure, responsive interface that bridges modern microservices and the 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe.

## Key Elements
- React SPA (SPA UI Components, Auth Guard Component)
- ASP.NET Core BFF (Claim Management Controller, Read Model Projections Cache Service, Mainframe Anti-Corruption Client, Audit Trail Service)
- Azure Cache for Redis
- Azure Active Directory & Key Vault
- Anti-Corruption Layer (Azure Functions & Azure Service Bus)

## Relationships
- React SPA -> Claim Management Controller [HTTPS / JSON]
- Claim Management Controller -> Read Model Projections Cache Service [.NET In-Memory / TCP over TLS]
- Claim Management Controller -> Audit Trail Service [.NET In-Memory]
- Audit Trail Service -> Anti-Corruption Layer [gRPC / HTTPS]
- Adjuster Web Application -> Azure Cache for Redis [TCP/Redis Protocol with TLS]
- Adjuster Web Application -> Azure Active Directory & Key Vault [OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect / Managed Identities]

## Technology Stack
- React SPA: Chosen for responsive UI and local session storage draft auto-saving.
- ASP.NET Core BFF: Implements server-side token management, FluentValidation, and API orchestration.
- Azure Cache for Redis: Caches claims data to guarantee sub-2-second screen loads (R-05).
- Azure Active Directory: Enforces Single Sign-On (R-07) and Role-Based Access Control.
- Azure Managed Identities: Eliminates hardcoded secrets for Key Vault and Redis connections.

## Rationale
This architecture isolates legacy mainframe latency using cached read models to meet strict performance SLAs. It securely maintains data consistency and user authorization while supporting a gradual 3-year migration path.

Claims Processing Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The modern platform incrementally replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system using a hybrid architecture in Azure West Europe. It ensures seamless online claim submission, real-time adjuster processing, and gradual claim-type migration with zero data loss.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Customers, Brokers, and Claims Adjusters
- **Gateways & Routing**: Azure API Management (Strangler Fig Router), React SPA Frontend, ASP.NET Core BFF
- **Backend Services**: Claims Processing Engine on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) containing Claim State Orchestrator, Migration Routing Component, and Reconciliation Worker
- **Integration & Messaging**: Anti-Corruption Layer (Azure Functions & Azure Service Bus)
- **Data & Security**: Azure SQL Database, Azure Cache for Redis, Azure Active Directory, Azure Key Vault, Azure Monitor & Managed Grafana

## Relationships
- Customers/Brokers & Adjusters -> Azure API Management: HTTPS/TLS 1.3
- Adjuster Web App -> ASP.NET Core BFF -> Claim State Orchestrator: HTTPS / REST / OAuth2/OIDC
- Claim State Orchestrator & Reconciliation Worker -> Azure SQL Database: TDS / EF Core
- Claims Processing Engine -> Anti-Corruption Layer: Azure Service Bus Topics (AMQP)
- Anti-Corruption Layer -> Legacy Mainframe: Legacy batch/sync protocols
- Reconciliation Worker -> Azure Monitor / Managed Grafana: OpenTelemetry / Prometheus metrics

## Technology Stack
- **Compute**: Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) for scalable microservices hosting
- **Backend Framework**: ASP.NET Core with MediatR for in-memory dispatching and Entity Framework Core
- **Database**: Azure SQL Database for ACID transactional persistence
- **Caching**: Azure Cache for Redis for performance optimization
- **Messaging**: Azure Service Bus for asynchronous event streaming
- **Observability**: OpenTelemetry, Azure Monitor, and Azure Managed Grafana for metrics
- **Security**: Azure Active Directory, Azure Key Vault CSI Driver, and Istio/Linkerd mTLS

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe dependencies while delivering sub-2-second adjuster response times via modern cloud services. It guarantees zero claim loss and rapid one-day rollback capabilities through dedicated reconciliation and routing components.

Anti-Corruption Layer.analysis:
## Overview
[The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a modern Azure-based platform. It ensures seamless hybrid operations, zero data loss, and incremental claim type migration over a three-year period.]

## Key Elements
[• Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL): Azure Functions & Azure Service Bus container insulating modern services from legacy structures.
• Translation Component: Azure Function mapping domain models to legacy COBOL schemas using Mapster/AutoMapper.
• Buffering & Routing Component: Azure Service Bus Topics/Queues managing asynchronous ingestion.
• Audit & Reconciliation Component: Cosmos DB and Azure Function capturing immutable payloads.
• Reconciliation & Alerting Component: Timer-triggered Azure Function executing discrepancy checks.]

## Relationships
[• Claims Processing Engine -> Translation Component: Publishes and consumes events via [Azure Service Bus, AMQP].
• Translation Component -> Legacy Mainframe: Synchronizes data via [HTTPS/SOAP, SFTP, and mTLS].
• Translation Component -> Audit & Reconciliation Component: Writes execution logs via [Internal .NET SDK / Cosmos DB API].
• Reconciliation & Alerting Component -> Azure Monitor: Emits operational alerts via [HTTPS / Azure Monitor API].]

## Technology Stack
[• Azure Functions (.NET 8 Isolated Worker Model): Chosen for serverless, event-driven scalability.
• Azure Service Bus: Selected for reliable asynchronous messaging and buffering.
• Cosmos DB: Utilized for immutable, high-performance audit log storage.
• Azure Key Vault & Managed Identities: Implemented for secure credential management and zero-trust authentication.]

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture mitigates high mainframe modification costs by isolating legacy interfaces within an auditable, secure Anti-Corruption Layer. It guarantees strict consistency and rapid rollback capabilities without disrupting core business operations.]

Azure Cache for Redis.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a hybrid cloud platform. It enables online claims submission and adjuster processing while maintaining data consistency during a multi-year migration.

## Key Elements
- **Customers & Brokers**: External users submitting claims online
- **Claims Adjusters**: Internal users managing claims via the new web application
- **Legacy Mainframe**: On-premise COBOL/DB2 system of record
- **Customer Portal**: React SPA hosted in Azure Static Web Apps
- **Adjuster Web Application**: React SPA + ASP.NET Core Backend-for-Frontend (BFF)
- **Claims Processing Engine**: ASP.NET Core Microservices on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
- **Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL)**: Azure Functions & Azure Service Bus
- **Azure Cache for Redis**: Standard Tier (C1/C2) with Claim State and Reference Data cache components
- **Azure API Management**: Strangler Fig Router
- **Security & Infrastructure**: Azure Active Directory, Azure Key Vault, Azure Private Link, and Azure Monitor Workbooks

## Relationships
- *Customers & Brokers* -> *Customer Portal*: Submits online claims [HTTPS]
- *Claims Adjusters* -> *Adjuster Web Application*: Manages claims [HTTPS]
- *Adjuster Web Application* -> *Azure Cache for Redis (Claim State Cache)*: Queries cached claims to meet sub-2s SLA [TCP/Redis Protocol over TLS 1.2/1.3]
- *Anti-Corruption Layer* -> *Azure Cache for Redis (Claim State Cache)*: Invalidates/updates cache via Pub/Sub on mainframe changes [TCP/Redis Protocol over TLS 1.2/1.3]
- *Claims Processing Engine* -> *Azure Cache for Redis (Reference Data Cache)*: Refreshes lookup data using cache-aside pattern [TCP/Redis Protocol over TLS 1.2/1.3]
- *Anti-Corruption Layer* -> *Legacy Mainframe*: Synchronizes claim data [MQ / Batch protocols]

## Technology Stack
- **Azure Cache for Redis**: Standard Tier for buffering slow mainframe responses and caching reference data
- **Microsoft Entra ID**: Used for secure authentication, RBAC, and least-privilege Redis access instead of static keys
- **Azure Private Link & Private Endpoints**: Isolates Redis from public internet exposure within internal VNets
- **Azure Monitor Workbooks**: Provides out-of-the-box operational dashboards for monitoring cache performance without complex cloud training
- **ASP.NET Core & Azure Functions**: Powers microservices and the anti-corruption layer

## Rationale
This architecture meets strict performance and consistency constraints by leveraging caching to hide mainframe latency while enforcing rigorous hybrid security boundaries. The design ensures seamless fallback capabilities within one day, accommodating the team's limited cloud experience.

Azure Active Directory & Key Vault.analysis:
## Overview
The system provides a hybrid insurance claims modernization platform, gradually replacing a legacy mainframe with modern cloud services while maintaining legacy operations. It ensures secure authentication, secrets management, and zero-loss claim processing during migration.

## Key Elements
- Token Service (Azure Entra ID)
- Secrets Provider (Azure Key Vault)
- Customer Portal (React SPA in Azure Static Web Apps)
- Adjuster Web Application (React SPA + ASP.NET Core BFF)
- Claims Processing Engine (ASP.NET Core Microservices on Azure Kubernetes Service)
- Anti-Corruption Layer (Azure Functions & Azure Service Bus)
- Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2)

## Relationships
- Customer Portal & Adjuster Web Application -> Token Service: Authenticates users and validates JWT tokens [HTTPS / OpenID Connect]
- Claims Processing Engine & Anti-Corruption Layer -> Secrets Provider: Retrieves secrets securely at runtime [HTTPS / Azure REST API via Azure Managed Identity]
- Anti-Corruption Layer <-> Legacy Mainframe: Synchronizes claims data [Batch / Asynchronous messaging]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Entra ID: Centralizes single sign-on and identity federation with on-premise Active Directory for R-07.
- Azure Key Vault: Secures runtime secrets and cryptographic keys using Private Endpoints to mitigate cloud-inexperience risks.
- Azure Managed Identities: Eliminates hardcoded credentials for microservices accessing Key Vault.
- ASP.NET Core / AKS: Powers modern claims processing microservices.

## Rationale
This architecture securely isolates identity and secrets management to support a cloud-inexperienced team while maintaining strict compliance. It enables gradual claim migration without extending the rigid nightly batch window.
